projects.title: Layer
projects.description: An MCP server that uses Tree-sitter AST navigation to slash token overhead and improve agent accuracy in large codebases.
projects.fullDescription:
### Why Layer
If you use coding agents like Claude Code or Cursor on production repositories, they default to naive file dumps, burning 100k+ tokens while losing architectural context. Agents often break downstream dependencies they cannot see, turning simple refactors into hallucination-prone guessing games. Layer mediates between the LLM and the filesystem via the Model Context Protocol, replacing bulk file reads with surgical symbol retrieval.

### Architecture & Implementation
Layer leverages Tree-sitter to perform incremental parsing of local source code. By maintaining an in-memory representation of the codebase, it performs AST traversal to map symbols, call sites, and definitions. This allows agents to request specific function slices or method implementations rather than entire files.

### Key Subsystems
- **Incremental AST Parser**: Updates symbol indices in sub-15ms bursts, ensuring the agent interacts with current code state without triggering full compiler rebuilds.
- **Call-Graph Navigator**: Tracks cross-file dependencies and imports, allowing agents to perform impact analysis before applying edits.
- **MCP Protocol Bridge**: Implements standard Model Context Protocol primitives to pipe structured code metadata into context-limited LLM windows.

### Performance & Benchmarks
In controlled benchmarks against the Ghidra codebase, Layer reduced total token consumption from 5.9M to 0.8M per task. This 87 percent reduction in input/reasoning overhead leads to nearly 3x faster resolution times for complex bug fixes.
features: Sub-15ms incremental syntax indexing via Tree-sitter ASTs
Automated call-graph analysis to prevent regression on downstream dependencies
Surgical symbol extraction to reduce context window pollution
Native MCP integration for compatibility with Claude and Cursor

projects.title: doc-engine
projects.description: A high performance headless document layout and vector rendering engine for React and TypeScript. Renders searchable vector PDF 1.7 streams and 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas previews without headless browsers or server daemons.
projects.category: Featured Open Source, Vector PDF Engine
projects.fullDescription: doc-engine (@worklabs05/doc-engine) is an open source headless document layout and vector rendering engine for React and TypeScript. Unlike traditional approaches that depend on bloated headless Chromium instances (Puppeteer) or heavy Python daemons, doc-engine calculates document layout coordinates in pure TypeScript and emits native vector PDF 1.7 operators and 60 FPS Canvas previews with zero server side overhead.
features: Emits native vector PDF 1.7 paths, text operators, and shapes (no rasterization)
Natural Top Left web coordinates (0,0) automatically converted to PDF standard Bottom Left coordinates
Multi page flow with automatic pagination and synchronized headers and footers
Real time 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas preview for instantaneous in browser rendering
Zero Puppeteer, zero Chromium, and zero Python daemon dependencies
Available on npm as @worklabs05/doc-engine with comprehensive documentation
